The RePORTER API caps result offsets well below NIH's annual award count, so
all-NIH questions need the **bulk ExPORTER files in DuckDB**. This notebook runs
the population-scale analyses directly against that store.

> **Prerequisite:** build the store first (one time, a few minutes):
> ```sh
> nih-agent bulk build 2000:2025        # awards (2.1M rows)
> nih-agent bulk build-pubs 2000:2025   # award→publication links (6.1M)
> ```

```{python}
import pandas as pd
from nih_science_agent.storage import duckdb_store

con = duckdb_store.connect()
print(con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM awards").fetchone()[0], "award rows")
print(con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM publinks").fetchone()[0], "publication links")
```

## Funding concentration (top-decile share + Gini)

How concentrated is NIH funding among investigators? Computed over *every* award,
not a sample.

```{python}
c = duckdb_store.funding_concentration(con, ic="NCI", year=2021, top_n=5)
print(f"NCI FY2021: {c.n_pis:,} contact PIs · ${c.total_funding:,.0f}")
print(f"  top 1% hold {c.top1_pct_share:.0%} · top 10% hold {c.top10_pct_share:.0%} · Gini {c.gini:.2f}")
pd.DataFrame(c.top_pis)
```

> The extreme top is inflated by large contracts/center grants attributed to one
> administrative contact PI — aggregate shares and Gini are the robust read.

## Diminishing returns at full scale

Linked-publications-per-\$ by PI funding quartile — the whole population, not the
48-PI sample of notebook 5.

```{python}
p = duckdb_store.funding_vs_output(con, ic="NCI", year=2010, funding_floor=250_000)
print(f"{p.n_pis:,} PIs · Spearman(support, pubs/$) = {p.spearman_funding_vs_pubs_per_dollar}")
pd.DataFrame([b.model_dump() for b in p.bins])[["label", "n_pis", "mean_funding", "mean_pubs", "mean_pubs_per_million"]]
```

## Output by FOA type (RFA vs PA)

```{python}
pd.DataFrame([r.model_dump() for r in duckdb_store.productivity_by_foa_type(con, ic="NCI", year=2010)])
```

## Grant → first-publication latency (with censoring)

```{python}
lat = duckdb_store.grant_to_output_latency(con, years=list(range(2005, 2013)))
print(f"{lat.grants_total:,} grants · {lat.grants_with_output:,} with a linked pub")
print(f"  median time to first publication: {lat.median_years_to_first_pub:.0f}y "
      f"(IQR {lat.p25_years:.0f}–{lat.p75_years:.0f}y)")
print(f"  {lat.pct_censored:.0%} censored (no linked pub — recent grants + incomplete linkage)")
con.close()
```

Censoring is reported, not hidden: silently dropping the ~40% of grants with no
linked publication would bias the median downward.
